label: Law determination controls checked
description: What a structure fixes about a probability law. One symmetry orbit fixes a unique law, but only the uniform one; a non-uniform law needs quantitative input. Positive binary switching fixes a unique stationary law, but only relative to the kernel's own masses: the kernel is itself a quantitative law, so stationarity relocates the law question to the kernel rather than answering it. Two orbits, zero switching or an idle upper mixture leave the law open. Uniqueness is not convergence (the flip kernel's point-mass orbit never reaches its unique stationary law). Generalizes #2144's exchange-symmetry control. Mathematics only: no claim that a source has such a structure, and no defeat of either the impersonal or the personal account. Not a transcription; establishes no premise.
